transcript: I love Groundhog Day. it is a musical that surprised me. when they first announced it, I was like, how are you going to adapt this into a musical? but I thought they did it beautifully. don't get me wrong, I don't super love the ending. I think seeing use one of the weakest songs in the show. and I also think playing Nancy is like, one of the worst act 2 openers of all time. but there is so much that that musical does right. one of the biggest challenges when you're adapting a well known film is how do you adapt the movie moments specifically for the stage? what they did in Groundhog Day is they didn't really word for word replicate any moments. they just replicated vibes. there's a scene that's often repeated in the film where he, like, interacts with the guy on the street. I think he's like an insurance guy. it's been a while since I saw the movie. that, for the most part, isn't in the musical. there's interactions similar to it, but it's definitely never happens word for word. one of the most memorable scenes in that film to me is the entire montage where he's trying to unalive himself, and they adapt that beautifully for the stage. none of that's replicated shot for a shot. there's a few that they try to replicate on the stage, but overall, it's all brand new. and Groundhog Day is similar to Legally Blonde and it does a great job of creating what I call montage songs, where you essentially take something that was originally a really cool movie montage, like the unaliving scene, and turn that into a song. and a hope is a perfect example of that. day has mostly montage songs where he's. he's going through multiple days in the span of a single song. not just in hope, but you have, you know, One Day. If I Had My Time Again, I Think is also a perfect montage song where you get to see the progression of her answer every time, depending on how the day is going. and overall, because they don't try to replicate the film beat for Beat, they do a perfect job in adapting that show for the stage.
